analysis.title: FactSet Research Systems Inc. (FDS): Investor day outlines AI strategy with modest growth and ambitious margin targets
key_insights: GS reiterates Sell on FDS with a 12-month price target of $237 against a $325.98 price (27.3% downside). Rating has been Sell since Jun 26, 2019.

FactSet's investor day introduced medium-term targets through F2029: ~6% organic revenue CAGR, adjusted operating margins above 36%, average FCF conversion above 90%, and ~10% annual adjusted EPS growth.

GS views the ~6% growth target as modest given the AI, enterprise agreement and consumption pricing initiatives, and the margin target as ambitious. FDS has needed elevated product development and compensation investment to sustain mid-single-digit growth, which contributed to margin contraction in recent years.
The F2029 margin target of above 36% compares with 34.5% in F2026, about 50 bps of expansion per year. The prior 2024 framework targeted 37-38% by F2028.

FDS identified $100mn+ of additional gross savings after $30mn in F2026, from operational streamlining, sales and marketing efficiency and more scalable technology and service infrastructure. Some savings will be reinvested in AI, compute, content and private markets, which GS says may constrain conversion to margin.

AI traction so far: AI offerings were 10%+ of F2026 net new ASV, and clients using AI solutions grew ASV twice as fast as other clients in F4Q 2026. About 650 clients used FactSet's MCP at the end of F2026.

MCP adopters' Workstation engagement rose to 92% from 89%. MCP clients generated ~10% ASV growth in F2026 vs just under 7% for clients without MCP. GS says the limited adoption history does not yet establish the durability or incremental contribution of AI-related growth.

FDS reported an internal benchmark in which its AI architecture delivered ~10% higher response quality at ~30% lower inference cost than a frontier-model harness accessing FDS data through MCP. One demonstrated workflow cut token requirements by up to 50x using structured sector knowledge.

The commercial model is moving from seat-based contracts to enterprise agreements and consumption pricing. More than 40% of F2026 renewals among the top 100 clients converted to enterprise agreements, and 80+ of the top 100 have consumption-linked arrangements. FDS did not quantify the pricing or discounting tied to the conversions.

GS flags a longer-term competitive risk: near-term MCP monetization may benefit from client experimentation, but vendor consolidation is a risk because FDS relies on third-party data that is neither exclusive nor created internally.

Client base: 9,000+ clients, ASV retention above 95%, top 100 clients about 39% of ASV. Clients using 5-7 product lines generate ~2.5x the net ASV expansion of single-product clients. Clients using 1-4 product lines contributed about half of F2026 ASV growth.

Efficiency evidence: headcount fell 3% in F2026 despite record organic ASV additions. AI generates 60%+ of committed code across measured repositories and resolves 30%+ of user-initiated support requests without human involvement.

Capital allocation: FCF above $700mn in F2026, share repurchases of $644mn (more than double the prior year), with a return toward a programmatic buyback pace expected over time. The dividend has risen for 27 consecutive years and gross leverage is targeted below 2.5x.
FDS reaffirmed F2027 guidance: 5.0-6.5% organic ASV growth, revenue of $2.600-2.625bn (5.0-6.0% growth), adjusted operating margin of 34.75-35.25% and adjusted EPS of $19.25-19.65.
GS estimates: F2027E revenue $2,621mn, adjusted EPS $19.61. F2028E revenue $2,778mn, EPS $21.54. F2029E revenue $2,949mn, EPS $23.85. The F2027E EPS is above the top of the guided range.

market_movers.rationale: Target is 11.0x NTM+1YR EPS of $23.41, a discount to the 18.4x Info Services peer median because of the shift to passive asset management and limited pricing increases. Price of $325.98 implies 27.3% downside.

sector_views.rationale: GS applies a discount to FDS versus the peer median for secular headwinds from passive asset management and limited pricing increases, partly offset by resilient, sticky revenue. This is a stock-level view, not a sector call.

earnings_insights: F2026 actuals (fiscal year ended Aug 2026): revenue $2,476.3mn (+6.7% y/y, all organic), adjusted operating margin 34.5%, adjusted EPS $18.01 (+6.1% y/y), FCF conversion 107%.

F2027 company guidance (reaffirmed at investor day): adjusted EPS $19.25-19.65, revenue $2.600-2.625bn, adjusted operating margin 34.75-35.25%, organic ASV growth 5.0-6.5%. GS estimates for F2027: adjusted EPS $19.61, revenue $2,621.2mn.
GS quarterly adjusted EPS estimates: Nov-26E $5.13, Feb-27E $4.98, May-27E $4.72, Aug-27E $4.78. F2026 quarterly actuals were $4.51, $4.46, $4.53 and $4.52.

GS adjusted EPS estimates: F2028E $21.54 (+9.8% y/y), F2029E $23.85 (+10.7% y/y). Medium-term company target is ~10% annual adjusted EPS growth through F2029, vs the prior framework of HSD-LDD growth.
Adjusted EBIT margin (GS) rises from 34.5% in F2026 to 35.0% F2027E, 35.5% F2028E and 36.1% F2029E, reaching the company's above-36% target only in F2029E.

trade_ideas.description: Sell/underweight FDS with a 12-month price target of $237
trade_ideas.rationale: Target multiple of 11.0x reflects a discount to peers for passive asset management headwinds and limited pricing increases.
trade_ideas.risk: Market share gains from improved functionality and competitive pricing, improved cross-selling and bundling, new product innovation, and faster margin expansion from cost efficiencies.

risk_factors: Upside risks to the Sell: (1) market share gains from improved functionality and competitive pricing, (2) improved cross-selling and bundling across the client base, (3) an expanded product portfolio from new product innovation, (4) faster margin expansion from cost efficiencies.
Continued investment in AI, compute, content and private markets may limit how much of the identified savings reaches margin.
Vendor consolidation creates a longer-term competitive risk because FDS relies on third-party data that is neither exclusive nor created internally.
The limited AI adoption history does not yet establish the durability or incremental contribution of AI-related growth.
FDS did not quantify the pricing or discounting associated with enterprise agreement conversions, so the incremental economics are unclear.
Secular shift to passive asset management and limited pricing increases weigh on the multiple.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 compares FactSet's F2026 actuals, F2027 guidance, the new F2029 medium-term outlook and the prior F2028 outlook: organic revenue growth 6.7% / 5-6% / ~6% CAGR, adjusted operating margin 34.5% / 34.75-35.25% / >36% vs prior 37-38%, adjusted EPS growth 6.1% / 7-9% / ~10% vs prior HSD-LDD, FCF conversion 107% / >90% average, gross leverage 1.5x / <2.5x vs prior 2.5x.
vol_and_positioning: FDS shares are up 14.7% over 3 months, 45.8% over 6 months and 23.0% over 12 months in absolute terms, as shown in the report's price performance table. Versus the S&P 500, the figures are +17.8%, +42.9% and +11.3%. The 3m ADTV is $241.7mn.
Price of $325.98 compares with the prior GS price-target-history closing prices of $269.95 (30-Sep-26) and $245.55 (1-Jul-26), a rise of about 21% since the last target update on Sep 30.

tension_points.bull_case: AI offerings were 10%+ of F2026 net new ASV, AI-adopting clients grew ASV twice as fast, MCP clients grew ~10% vs just under 7% for non-MCP clients, and FDS says faster AI and consumption adoption is upside not embedded in its targets.
tension_points.bear_case: GS says the limited adoption history does not establish durability, MCP monetization may be flattered by client experimentation, and vendor consolidation is a longer-term risk because FDS relies on third-party data that is neither exclusive nor created internally.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS lists market share gains from improved functionality and competitive pricing, better cross-selling and bundling, and faster margin expansion from cost efficiencies as the risks to its Sell.

tension_points.bull_case: FDS identified $100mn+ of gross savings, headcount fell 3% in F2026 despite record organic ASV additions, and AI resolves 30%+ of support requests without human involvement.
tension_points.bear_case: GS calls the above-36% target ambitious because FDS has needed elevated product development and compensation investment to sustain mid-single-digit growth, and continued AI, compute, content and private markets spending may constrain conversion.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An increased pace of margin expansion driven by cost efficiencies, named by GS as an upside risk to its Sell.
